findings.source_quote: καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ
findings.english_quote: and, of prophecies, obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things
findings.issue: All surviving wording is represented, but this sequence remains an untranslated syntactic fragment. The English does not establish what is asserted about the obscure and ambiguous things, how they relate to the preceding statement that foreknowledge needs nothing for comprehension, or what predication the contrast with explicit and plain things corrects. The purpose clause is individually intelligible, but its attachment does not resolve those missing relations. The notes honestly disclose this failure, and the conjectural repair has not been imported; neither fact makes the main rendering adequate. The block concerns unresolved clause meaning, not merely competing interpretations or uncertainty about the verified print.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a defensible grammatical and contextual account of the unchanged wording: explain the function of προφητειῶν, the predicate or justified ellipsis governing the contrasted neuter expressions, and the scope of ἀλλὰ. An unprinted predicate is not automatically impermissible if ordinary ellipsis supports it, but any supplied predicate or negative scope must be justified independently of the proposed καὶ οὐ προφητεύει conjecture. Until that account supports an intelligible English rendering, retain the block. No renewed print verification is warranted merely by this construction's difficulty; any replacement must receive fresh review.
